correctness.rationale: For five distinct nodes the complex five-by-five Fourier Vandermonde is invertible. An exact cardinal-Laurent formula reduces each weight sign to cos(Delta)+2cos(x)cos(y) with strictly positive denominator. Four signed derivatives prove a global extremum at the alternating perturbation endpoints for every radius up to 1/4, giving the exact zero at alpha*=0.2014594224605106. For any larger allowed radius use a smaller counterexample radius below 1/4. The included standard-library verifier passed 1059 finite Fourier-exactness and sign comparisons; these only sanity-check the universal analytic proof.

value.rationale: Exactly five nodes are the natural minimum samples for exact integration of the five-dimensional trigonometric degree-two space with unique interpolatory weights. Nonnegativity prevents a normalized positive integrand from yielding a negative quadrature result. An explicit sharp worst-case independently bounded node-displacement radius, and its extremal pattern, answers a concrete robustness design question not supplied by random-oversampling existence or large-N counterexamples. The result is a complete natural finite-grid classification rather than an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
